svg.text: The ADA node's protocol stack
Two channels cross the network. The detector reaches the ADA Core through a pipe, not as a network peer.
CARRIED
the payload — not a layer
object message (R2) · v2x_object
one perceived-object update, relayed inward
warning message (R4)
risk state, scene, and the track record embedded
Application
OSI 7
Transport
OSI 4
Network
OSI 3
Link
OSI 2
UTF-8 JSON, one object per datagram
parsed by nlohmann/json into the object-message binding
unknown fields ignored
UTF-8 JSON, one object per datagram
built by nlohmann/json from the warning binding
the track record nested inside it
no retransmission, no ordering, no framing
one message per datagram, fire and forget
IPv4 · static addresses on 10.99.0.0/24, this node at 10.99.0.12
no routing and no gateway — every peer is on the one subnet
Simulated Ethernet · the CarSky Ethernet Bridge node, one L2 segment
the pod has no physical interface; the bridge is the medium
Outside the stack — the detector channel
track record (R3) · TrackedObject
an application-layer message, and nothing below it
The ADA Core — the node's C++ process — spawns the detector as a child process in the same container: argv in, exit code out, track records on standard output.
An OS pipe supplies no addressing, no ports and no message framing, so newlines delimit the messages and nothing sits beneath the JSON.
The pipe is ordered and lossless, and blocks when its buffer fills, where UDP would discard the datagram.
